title: NECO SSCE
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the public NECO SSCE syllabus. Not a capture of past exam questions.

items.stem: The new teacher spoke to the pupils with such conviction that even the most restless child fell silent and listened.
items.explanation: The sentence shows the teacher held the pupils' attention firmly, so the quality that fits is conviction. Hesitation, confusion and indifference would all weaken her hold on the class.

items.stem: The chairman's remarks were terse. Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word terse.
items.explanation: Terse means using few words and cutting straight to the point. The other options describe the opposite qualities of length, gentleness or vagueness.

items.stem: The committee were divided in their opinions when the vote was finally taken on the proposal.
items.explanation: When a collective noun such as committee acts as separate individuals who disagree, British usage takes a plural verb, so were is correct. The singular forms would treat the group as one unit.

items.stem: To let the cat out of the bag means to
options: release an animal from a cage
begin a quarrel with a neighbour
items.explanation: The idiom means to disclose a secret, often by accident. It has nothing to do with animals, quarrels or abandoning plans, which are literal or unrelated readings.

items.stem: Neither the principal nor the teachers were present at the assembly yesterday morning.
items.explanation: With neither...nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, which is teachers (plural), so were is correct. The singular forms would agree with principal instead.

items.stem: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word meticulous as used in the passage.
items.explanation: Meticulous describes a person who shows great attention to detail. Carelessness, generosity and a quarrelsome nature are unrelated traits.

items.stem: The rain had barely stopped when the children rushed out to play in the flooded street.
items.explanation: The construction barely...when links two events happening almost at once, so when is correct. Than follows comparatives, while then and that do not fit this structure.

items.stem: The accused man was released from custody for lack of sufficient evidence to charge him.
items.explanation: The fixed expression is for lack of, meaning because there was not enough of something. The other prepositions do not form this standard collocation.

items.stem: The word record is stressed on the first syllable when it is used as a noun rather than a verb.
items.explanation: Many two-syllable words stress the first syllable as nouns and the second as verbs, so record as a noun takes first-syllable stress. Prepositions and conjunctions do not carry this stress pattern.

items.stem: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word frugal as used in the sentence about the family.
items.explanation: Frugal means careful and economical in spending. Wastefulness is its opposite, and wealth or dishonesty are not implied by the word.

items.stem: The two brothers resemble each other very closely in both appearance and manner.
items.explanation: Each other is used for two people, while one another is preferred for more than two, so each other is correct here. Themselves is reflexive and each another is not a standard form.

items.stem: Although he was exhausted after the journey, he still refused to ask anyone for help.
items.explanation: The word although introduces a contrast, so a tiring state such as exhausted fits the sense of struggling on. Energetic, cheerful and confident would not create the intended contrast.

items.stem: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word benevolent as used in the passage.
items.explanation: Benevolent means kind and wishing to do good, so its opposite is cruel and unkind. Kind and generous is a synonym, and the other pairs describe unrelated qualities.

items.stem: The manager, together with his assistants, is attending the conference in the capital next week.
items.explanation: A phrase beginning with together with does not change the number of the subject, so the singular manager takes is. The plural forms wrongly treat the assistants as part of the subject.

items.stem: The boy said, I will come tomorrow. In reported speech this becomes The boy said that he would come the following day.
items.explanation: When a present-tense promise is reported, will changes to would and tomorrow becomes the following day. Keeping will ignores the backshift required by reported speech.

items.stem: Simplify the expression (2 raised to the power 3 multiplied by 2 raised to the power 4) divided by 2 raised to the power 5.
items.explanation: Adding the indices when multiplying gives 2^7, and subtracting the index when dividing gives 2^2, which equals 4. The other values come from adding or subtracting the wrong powers.

items.stem: If 3x minus 7 equals 11, find the value of x.
items.explanation: Adding 7 to both sides gives 3x = 18, so x = 6. The other options result from adding or dividing the wrong quantities.

items.stem: Find the highest common factor of 24 and 36.
items.explanation: The common factors of 24 and 36 include 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12, of which 12 is the greatest. The number 6 is common but not the highest, while 72 is a common multiple.

items.stem: A trader bought an article for 800 naira and sold it for 1000 naira. Calculate the percentage profit made.
items.explanation: Profit is 200 naira on a cost price of 800 naira, and 200 divided by 800 gives 0.25 or 25 percent. Dividing by the selling price instead gives the wrong 20 percent.

items.stem: Find the value of x in the equation 2x plus 3y equals 12 when y equals 2.
items.explanation: Substituting y = 2 gives 2x + 6 = 12, so 2x = 6 and x = 3. The other options come from substituting y incorrectly or misdividing.

items.stem: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2 to 3 to 4. Find the size of the largest angle.
items.explanation: The ratio parts sum to 9, and each part is 180 divided by 9, which is 20 degrees. The largest angle is 4 parts, that is 80 degrees.

items.stem: If the mean of the numbers 4, 7, x and 9 is 8, find the value of x.
items.explanation: A mean of 8 over four numbers gives a total of 32, and 4 + 7 + 9 = 20, so x = 12. The other values give the wrong total.

items.stem: Calculate the area of a circle of radius 7 cm, taking pi as 22 over 7.
items.explanation: Area equals pi times radius squared, so 22/7 times 49 equals 154 square cm. Using the diameter or forgetting to square the radius gives the other values.

items.stem: Solve the quadratic equation x squared minus 5x plus 6 equals 0.
options: x equals minus 2 or x equals minus 3
items.explanation: Factorising gives (x - 2)(x - 3) = 0, so x = 2 or x = 3. The pair 1 and 6 multiplies to 6 but does not sum to 5.

items.stem: Express the decimal number 0.75 as a fraction in its lowest terms.
items.explanation: 0.75 equals 75/100, which reduces to 3/4 by dividing both parts by 25. The other fractions have different decimal values.

items.stem: A fair coin is tossed once. What is the probability of obtaining a head?
items.explanation: There are two equally likely outcomes, head and tail, so the probability of a head is one half. A quarter would apply only to a more restricted event.

items.stem: Find the simple interest on 5000 naira for 2 years at 10 percent per annum.
items.explanation: Simple interest is principal times rate times time, that is 5000 times 0.10 times 2, which equals 1000 naira. Omitting the time or the rate gives the other values.

items.stem: Simplify the fraction three quarters divided by nine sixteenths.
items.explanation: Dividing by a fraction multiplies by its reciprocal, so 3/4 times 16/9 equals 48/36, which simplifies to 4/3. Multiplying without inverting gives 27/64.

items.stem: Find the next term of the number sequence 2, 6, 12, 20, and so on.
items.explanation: The differences between successive terms are 4, 6 and 8, so the next difference is 10 and the next term is 30. The other options ignore the increasing differences.

items.stem: In a right-angled triangle the two shorter sides are 3 cm and 4 cm. Find the length of the hypotenuse.
items.explanation: By Pythagoras' theorem the hypotenuse squared is 9 + 16 = 25, so the hypotenuse is 5 cm. Adding the sides directly gives the incorrect 7 cm.

items.stem: The organelle responsible for the synthesis of proteins in a living cell is the
items.explanation: Ribosomes are the sites of protein synthesis. Mitochondria release energy, lysosomes digest materials and the nucleolus helps form ribosomes rather than synthesising protein directly.

items.stem: The process by which green plants manufacture their own food using sunlight is known as
items.explanation: Photosynthesis uses light energy to build food from carbon dioxide and water. Respiration releases energy, transpiration loses water and digestion breaks food down.

items.stem: One major function of the red blood cell in the human body is to
options: clot blood at the site of a wound
items.explanation: Red blood cells contain haemoglobin, which carries oxygen to the tissues. Antibody production and engulfing bacteria are done by white cells, and clotting by platelets.

items.stem: The basic unit of inheritance that is passed from parents to offspring is the
items.explanation: A gene is the unit of hereditary material that carries a trait from one generation to the next. Cells, tissues and organs are structural levels, not units of inheritance.

items.stem: The part of the human ear that is mainly responsible for balance and body equilibrium is the
items.explanation: The semi-circular canals detect changes in the position of the head and control balance. The ear drum, ossicles and pinna are concerned with hearing or collecting sound.

items.stem: In flowering plants the main route for the loss of water vapour and gaseous exchange is the
items.explanation: Stomata are tiny openings, mostly on leaves, through which water vapour leaves and gases are exchanged. Root hairs and xylem absorb or conduct water, and phloem transports food.

items.stem: The organism that transmits the malaria parasite from one person to another is the
items.explanation: The female Anopheles mosquito transmits the malaria parasite when it bites. Houseflies spread other diseases, the tsetse fly transmits sleeping sickness and Culex mosquitoes transmit filariasis.

items.stem: The blood group that is often called the universal donor because its cells carry no antigens A or B is
items.explanation: Group O red cells have neither A nor B antigens, so they can be given to patients of the other groups. Group AB is instead called the universal recipient.

items.stem: The mode of nutrition in which an organism feeds on dead and decaying organic matter is described as
items.explanation: Saprophytes obtain nutrients by digesting dead and decaying matter externally. Holozoic nutrition involves ingesting food, parasites feed on living hosts and autotrophs make their own food.

items.stem: The structure that prevents food from entering the windpipe during swallowing is the
items.explanation: The epiglottis covers the opening of the trachea as food is swallowed, directing it into the oesophagus. The larynx is the voice box and the oesophagus carries food to the stomach.

items.stem: The part of the leaf where most photosynthesis takes place is the
items.explanation: The palisade mesophyll lies near the upper surface and has many chloroplasts, so most photosynthesis occurs there. The epidermis and cuticle are protective layers.

items.stem: The enzyme present in human saliva that begins the digestion of starch is
items.explanation: Salivary amylase starts the breakdown of starch into simpler sugars in the mouth. Pepsin and trypsin act on proteins in the stomach and intestine, and lipase digests fats.

items.stem: A group of organisms of the same species living together in a particular habitat is called a
items.explanation: A population is all the members of one species in a habitat. A community contains many species, while an ecosystem and a biome include the physical environment as well.

items.stem: The type of cell division that produces gametes with half the normal chromosome number is
items.explanation: Meiosis halves the chromosome number and forms gametes. Mitosis gives identical body cells, while binary fission and budding are forms of asexual reproduction.

items.stem: A deficiency of vitamin C in the human diet causes the disease known as
items.explanation: Lack of vitamin C causes scurvy, with bleeding gums and poor healing. Rickets is caused by lack of vitamin D, beri-beri by lack of vitamin B and night blindness by lack of vitamin A.

items.stem: The chemical symbol for the element sodium is
items.explanation: Sodium has the symbol Na, from its Latin name natrium. Sn is the symbol for tin, and So and Sd are not symbols of any element.

items.stem: Which of the following elements is a noble gas with a completely filled outer shell?
items.explanation: Argon is a noble gas with a full outer shell, which is why it is unreactive. Chlorine and oxygen are reactive non-metals and sodium is a reactive metal.

items.stem: The change of a solid directly into a gas without first becoming a liquid is called
items.explanation: Sublimation is the direct change from solid to gas, as shown by iodine and dry ice. Evaporation and melting involve the liquid and solid states respectively, and condensation is gas to liquid.

items.stem: The atomic number of an element is defined as the number of
options: protons and neutrons in its nucleus
items.explanation: The atomic number equals the number of protons in the nucleus and is the same as the number of electrons in a neutral atom. The proton plus neutron total is the mass number.

items.stem: Which of the following substances acts as an oxidizing agent in a chemical reaction?
items.explanation: Oxygen accepts electrons and so acts as an oxidizing agent. Hydrogen, carbon and sodium are typically reducing agents because they tend to lose electrons and be oxidised.

items.stem: The pH value of a neutral solution at 25 degrees Celsius is
items.explanation: A neutral solution has a pH of 7 at this temperature. Values below 7 are acidic and values above 7 are alkaline, so 1, 14 and 0 represent acidic or strongly alkaline solutions.

items.stem: The gas evolved when dilute hydrochloric acid reacts with zinc metal is
items.explanation: A metal above hydrogen in the activity series displaces hydrogen from an acid, so zinc gives off hydrogen. Oxygen, chlorine and carbon dioxide are not produced in this reaction.

items.stem: Avogadro's number, the number of particles in one mole of a substance, is approximately
items.explanation: One mole contains about 6.02 x 10^23 particles, known as Avogadro's number. The other values are the wrong order of magnitude or belong to other constants such as the electron charge.

items.stem: The type of bond formed by the complete transfer of electrons from a metal atom to a non-metal atom is
items.explanation: Transfer of electrons from a metal to a non-metal produces oppositely charged ions held by ionic bonding. Covalent bonding shares electrons, metallic bonding occurs in metals and hydrogen bonding is a weak attraction between molecules.

items.stem: The correct chemical formula for tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid, commonly called sulphuric acid, is
items.explanation: Sulphuric acid has the formula H2SO4, with two replaceable hydrogen atoms and four oxygen atoms. H2SO3 is sulphurous acid and H2S is hydrogen sulphide.

items.stem: The most suitable method for separating an insoluble solid such as sand from water is
items.explanation: Filtration traps the insoluble sand in the filter paper while water passes through. Distillation and evaporation are used to recover dissolved solids or the liquid itself.

items.stem: Elements placed in the same group of the periodic table have the same number of
items.explanation: Members of a group share the same number of outer-shell electrons, which gives them similar chemical properties. The number of shells increases down a group and the proton number differs from element to element.

items.stem: The reaction between an acid and a base to produce a salt and water is known as
items.explanation: Neutralization is the reaction of an acid with a base to give a salt and water. Oxidation involves electron loss, polymerization joins monomers and fermentation breaks down sugars.

items.stem: Which of the following substances is commonly used as a reducing agent in the extraction of metals?
items.explanation: Carbon is used to reduce metal oxides in extraction because it readily loses electrons and removes oxygen. Oxygen and chlorine are oxidizing agents, and sulphur is not a typical reducing agent for metal oxides.

items.stem: The relative molecular mass of carbon(IV) oxide, whose formula is CO2, is
items.explanation: Carbon has an atomic mass of 12 and each oxygen atom 16, so 12 + 16 + 16 equals 44. The value 32 is the mass of one oxygen molecule and 28 is the mass of carbon monoxide.
